The PULP-score (Peptic Ulcer Perforation score) is a prognostic clinical assessment tool designed to predict mortality in patients who have suffered a perforated peptic ulcer [^src1]. It was developed in conjunction with the PULP trial and serves as a core component of the scientific foundation for the Akut Kirurgi Databasen (Danish Clinical Register of Emergency Surgery) [^src1]. Within the context of the database's annual quality reports, the PULP-score and its associated trial data underpin the evidence-based standards used to evaluate outcome quality, including 30-day and 90-day mortality rates, across the entire patient journey from hospital arrival to postoperative care [^src1].
